question: Analyzing the diplomatic friction between French commanders: The failure of the French to consolidate their hold on Madras in 1746 was primarily due to a diplomatic and personal clash between Dupleix and La Bourdonnais. What was the core issue of their dispute?
options: La Bourdonnais wanted to annex Madras to Mauritius, while Dupleix wanted to hand it to the Dutch
La Bourdonnais wished to ransom Madras back to the English for a private payment, whereas Dupleix insisted on holding it or destroying it to eliminate English power
Dupleix wanted to restore the Nawab of Arcot to Madras, while La Bourdonnais wanted to declare himself Sultan
La Bourdonnais was in secret league with Robert Clive to divide the Carnatic
explanation: After capturing Madras in 1746, La Bourdonnais, who believed his naval mission was temporary, agreed to restore Madras to the English in exchange for a large ransom (and a personal bribe). Dupleix, who wanted to completely eradicate the British presence in the Carnatic, vehemently opposed this treaty, asserting his supreme authority in India. This bitter dispute allowed the English time to recover and caused La Bourdonnais to leave with his fleet, exposing the French to naval vulnerability.
